introduction.title: Welcome to Lekana API
introduction.content: The Lekana API allows you to programmatically interact with our document processing engine. You can trigger workflows, check execution status, and retrieve processed data seamlessly from your own applications. Our API is built on RESTful principles, using standard HTTP methods and JSON for communication.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.content: To authenticate with the Lekana API, you must include your private API key in the `X-API-Key` header of every request. You can manage your API keys in the developer settings of your Lekana dashboard. Treat your API key as a secret—never share it or commit it to version control.

core_concepts.title: Workflows
core_concepts.content: A workflow is a sequence of actions defined in the Lekana editor. Each workflow has a unique ID and must be published before it can be triggered via the API.

core_concepts.title: Executions
core_concepts.content: When you run a workflow, an 'Execution' is created. This process is asynchronous. The API will return an `executionId` which you can use to poll for status or receive results via webhooks.

categories.name: Workflows
categories.description: Trigger and manage your document processing pipelines.

endpoints.name: Run Workflow (URL)
endpoints.description: Trigger a workflow using documents hosted at public URLs.
endpoints.long_description: Use this endpoint when you already have your documents hosted online. It accepts a JSON payload containing a message and document URLs. The message will be passed as an input variable to your workflow.

headers.description: Specifies that the request body is in JSON format.
Your unique API key for authentication.

fields.name: input.message
fields.description: A message or prompt that will be passed to the workflow as an input variable.

fields.name: documents
fields.description: An array of document objects. Each object must contain 'url', 'filename', and 'mimeType'.

responses.description: Accepted - The workflow execution has successfully started.

endpoints.name: Run Workflow (File Upload)
endpoints.description: Trigger a workflow by uploading document files directly.
endpoints.long_description: Use this endpoint to upload files directly from your application. This endpoint requires a multipart/form-data request body containing the files and an optional message.

headers.description: Specifies that the request contains file data.
Your unique API key for authentication.

fields.name: message
fields.description: The message or prompt to pass to the workflow.

fields.name: files
fields.description: One or more files to be processed by the workflow.

responses.description: Accepted - Files uploaded and workflow started.

error_codes.description: The request was malformed or missing required parameters.
The API key is missing or invalid.
The requested workflow or resource does not exist.
